instruction: Navigate to your email's Bills folder, find the latest email, and launch its first link using Chrome.

metadata.explanation: Rephrased instruction for the same task. Steps: 1) Open Thunderbird and navigate to Bills folder, 2) Select the most recent email (AWS invoice), 3) Click the Amazon.com URL to open in Chrome. The evaluator uses existing functions to verify 3 tabs are open with correct URLs.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the final state: 3 Chrome tabs open with expected URLs (apple.com, scholar.google.com, amazon.com)
Getter function get_open_tabs_info correctly extracts all open tabs with URLs from Chrome
Metric function is_expected_tabs correctly compares expected URLs against actual open tabs
Expected values are semantically correct: 2 pre-configured tabs + 1 new tab from email link
Data flow is logically sound: getter extracts tab info → metric compares URLs → returns pass/fail
Limitation: Only verifies final state, not intermediate steps (Bills folder navigation, latest message selection)
Limitation: Cannot distinguish between manually opening amazon.com vs clicking email link
Acceptable for OSWorld: Final state verification is standard practice when setup provides specific environment state
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding verification that Thunderbird Bills folder was accessed (though not critical for final state verification)
Could enhance by checking that only 3 tabs exist (not just that 3 expected tabs are present)
Current evaluator is adequate for task verification given standard OSWorld evaluation patterns
